g.text: Five ways to send a bit, and what each costs
Rows: the schemes. Columns: what the FPGA does, where the carrier goes, what the receiver's I/Q and comparators see, the spectrum, the SNR each needs, how far it reaches. sim/link_rates.py.

g.text: Idle carrier against a whitened stream: which is lower latency, which is more robust
IDLE CARRIER + EVENTS (this board's native mode): the carrier is always on; a bit is a phase (or frequency) change at the instant the FPGA pin moves; the receiver's comparator reports it as soon
as the 100 MHz arm filter settles (3.5 ns). There is no symbol clock, no slot to wait for, no frame. The price: while idle, every noise excursion past the comparator is a false bit, so the link
must be QUIET: ≤ 1e-4 errors per decision (1e4 false events/s at 100 MHz; 1 in 100 trials at 1 MHz) → BPSK needs 11.4 dB, not the 7.3 dB that 1 %% message errors would. The gateware's dwell
requirement (a flip must persist N samples) trades latency for quiet.
WHITENED STREAM (an LFSR-scrambled continuous BPSK at 100 Mbaud): the receiver recovers a symbol clock from the transitions, integrates each symbol (a matched filter) and descrambles. Same energy
per decision as the idle carrier (the arm filter IS a one-symbol matched filter), so no sensitivity gain; a self-synchronising descrambler triples the errors; the bit waits for the next slot
(5 ns average) and a full symbol (10 ns): +13 ns of latency; the transmitter is always 200 MHz wide (it interferes with every WiFi channel it touches, and it is what §15.247 wants a digital
transmitter to look like). It does NOT help against interference: spreading gain is zero when chips = bits. Where it helps: when the receiver is a conventional slotted detector that needs a
clock; a continuous quality estimate. Both run on this hardware unchanged (the FPGA drives the ladders), so the comparison is an experiment, not a design decision. Interference robustness
comes from elsewhere: the arm bandwidth (narrower = quieter = slower), the antennas' directivity (24 dBi panels reject 20-30 dB off-axis), transmit power, and the channel (UNII-2C 5.47-5.725 GHz
is nearly empty indoors; scan with the B210 first).

Range at which BPSK stays quiet (1e-4 per decision), metres: the fast path (flags) / the slow path (confirms), with the old OOK link in brackets. Free space + margin; the shorter of noise and the comparator floor.
scenario board alone2 W module at +30 dBm (20 dB pad) 2 W module at its P1dB (+33) 10 W amplifier (+40)
campus: panels, 10 m cables, amplifiers at the board 3077 / 11 km (2263) 31 km / >100 km (23 km) 44 km / >100 km (33 km) 99 km / >100 km (73 km)
campus: panels, PA and LNA at the panel 17 km / 63 km (13 km) >100 km / >100 km (>100 km) >100 km / >100 km (>100 km) >100 km / >100 km (>100 km)
mountain: 30 dBi dishes, PA and LNA at the dish 69 km / >100 km (50 km) >100 km / >100 km (>100 km) >100 km / >100 km (>100 km) >100 km / >100 km (>100 km)

Through walls at 30 m with whips and no amplifier the slow path has 18 dB to spare (drywall 3-6 dB, brick 10-15, a floor 15-25). The USB-C amplifier's output is a guess until measured: the TX MON jack and the ADC read it.
